ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture shows five face-up cards. The top row has cards labeled P and Q. The bottom row has cards labeled 3, 4, and 6. Reasoning: Jane's statement is a conditional rule: if a card has a vowel on one side, then the other side must have an even number. To prove this false, Mary needs to find a card with a vowel on one side and an odd number on the other. Of the visible cards, 3 is the only odd number. If the other side of the 3 card is a vowel, then Jane's rule is false. Therefore Mary should turn over the 3 card.

method.method_draft: Begin by listing the visible cards from the image: P and Q are letter cards, while 3, 4, and 6 are number cards. Use elimination. Turning over P or Q cannot disprove the rule because P and Q are not vowels, so Jane's statement says nothing about them. Turning over 4 or 6 cannot immediately show a violation because they are even numbers; even if a vowel is on the other side, that would satisfy the rule, not refute it. The only remaining card that could violate the rule is 3, because an odd number paired with a vowel would contradict Jane's claim. Thus Mary should turn over 3.
